heads.text: FORT MOURNS ONE OF ITS OWN
A CHAIR SITS EMPTY IN THE DINING HALL
THE FORT IS ONE DWARF QUIETER TONIGHT
OBITUARY DESK: A LIFE OF HONEST WORK
SAD NEWS FROM THE LOWER LEVELS

reads.text: We begin tonight with sad news. {name}, {prof}, has died. DNN extends its condolences to everyone who ever shared a mug with them.
{name} the {prof} is dead. We are told the fort's coffin makers have been informed, and that they are taking it personally.
Confirmed reports now: {name} has passed. The {prof}'s workshop is quiet tonight, and so, for once, is this newsroom.
{anchor} here. We've lost {name}: {prof} by trade, neighbour by choice, and by every account a dwarf who never left a door open in winter.
The fort is down to {pop} tonight. One of the dwarves who made it more than a number has died.
We are getting word that a citizen of {fort} has died. Details are still coming in. For now, the newsroom asks you to raise a mug.
{name} has died. Sources close to the tavern say a seat at the corner table will be left empty, and that nobody is to argue about it.
A sombre {season} in {fort}. {name}, {prof}, will not be coming back up the stairs. We'll have more as the details reach us.
{citizen} was among the first to hear the news, and has asked that the fort remember {name} for the work, not the ending.
There is no easy way to read this one. We have lost a citizen tonight. The masons have been asked to cut a slab, and to take their time.
The {year} obituary column grows by one. {name} the {prof} has died, and DNN will be keeping the lamp lit at the desk tonight.
Death has come to {fort}. We will not speculate on the cause on air. We will only say: check your stairs, check your levers, hug your cat.
{name} has died this {month}. Colleagues describe a stubborn, reliable dwarf who was the only one who ever cleaned up after the forge.
For those just joining us: a dwarf of {fort} has died. Coverage will continue, quietly. Please keep the noise down near the tombs.

heads.text: FROM PET TO PROVISIONS? DNN INVESTIGATES

reads.text: {name} has died. The {creature} was well liked, had no enemies, and only rarely stood in a doorway for an entire season.
We can confirm the death of {name}. The owner asks for privacy and, if at all possible, that it not be served at the next feast.
Sad scenes at the pasture as {name} the {creature} passed on. The other animals have been informed. They did not react, as is their way.
Reports from the butcher's shop suggest the {creature} known as {name} may have been slaughtered. DNN asks: was it worth it? The butcher says yes.
An animal has died in {fort}. The pasture is a little quieter tonight, which the herders say is the first time that's ever been a bad thing.
{name} is no more. Fort cats were seen gathering near the spot, and we're told it was respect and not, as some claim, opportunism.
Word now from the kennels: {name} has passed. Trainers describe the {creature} as loyal, brave, and terrible at fetch.
A death in the animal community this {season}. The tanner is said to be sombre, but also, quietly, measuring.
{citizen} has confirmed the death of a much-loved animal and asks the fort to stop suggesting stew. At least for a day.
Breaking from the pasture: {name} has died. Experts remind us that every {creature} is someone's favourite, even the ones that bite.
We have lost {name}. The {creature} leaves behind a grazing spot, a water trough, and a dwarf who refuses to talk about it.
A pet has died in {fort}. As is tradition, its owner will now spend some days staring at a wall. Please give them the wall.
{name} has gone to the great pasture beneath the mountain. Note: that's not a real place. We checked. Engineering wants to dig one.
Livestock figures are down by one tonight. Behind that number, sources say, was a face. A slightly dim, very loved face.

heads.text: NEW CITIZEN ARRIVES, SMALL AND LOUD
FORT GROWS BY ONE TINY BEARD
A NEW FACE IN THE HALLS
WELCOME TO THE MOUNTAIN, LITTLE ONE
THE FORT HAS A NEW RESIDENT

reads.text: {name} has given birth. Mother and baby are doing well, and the baby is reportedly already disappointed in the ale ration.
Joyful news: {name} has had a baby. The newest citizen of {fort} has no profession, no opinions, and a very powerful voice.
We're getting reports of a birth in the bedroom district. {fort} grows to {pop}, and the halls get noticeably louder.
Congratulations to {name}! DNN is told the baby has its mother's eyes and, alarmingly, its grandfather's beard.
A baby has been born in {fort} this {season}. The carpenters say they'll have a cradle ready by the time it's walking. Probably.
{name} welcomed a child today. The infant was immediately carried back to work, as is the proud dwarven way.
Our {month} birth announcement: {name} is a mother. Early polling suggests the baby is the most popular dwarf in the fort.
There's a new dwarf in the mountain. We don't know its name yet. Neither, we suspect, does it.
{name} has delivered a healthy baby. The hospital staff, unused to good news, are said to be confused but pleased.
Birth confirmed. {citizen} is already offering to teach the child mining, which the family has declined until it can stand.
{name} is a mother tonight. Analysts expect a sharp rise in nap demand and a modest decline in sleep across the bedroom sector.
Good news for once, viewers. A baby! In {fort}! {anchor2}, you may cheer on air.
{name} has had a little one. The child reportedly bit the midwife, and the fort is calling it a strong start.
A birth in {fort}, and the {year} census team has thrown out its numbers again. They'd like everyone to stop doing this mid-count.

heads.text: BEDROOM SHORTAGE FEARED AS MIGRANTS POUR IN
NEW HANDS, NEW BEARDS, NEW PROBLEMS

reads.text: We're getting reports of {count} migrants at the gate. Most are carrying everything they own. One is carrying a single sock.
A new wave of migrants has arrived in {fort}. Officials remind newcomers that the good bedrooms are taken and the bad ones are also taken.
{count} dwarves have walked into {fort} today, bringing the population to {pop}. The dining hall manager has been seen breathing into a bag.
Migrants! Early interviews suggest most of them are fish dissectors, which is exactly what the fort did not ask for.
The migrants are here. {reporter} is at the gate, where we're told the newcomers are already asking where the tavern is.
Breaking: {count} new citizens this {season}. The bookkeeper has asked everyone to please hold still while they are counted.
Fresh faces at the entrance today. {citizen} greeted them personally, then remembered there were no jobs to hand out.
A migrant wave has reached {fort}. Sources say several are already stuck behind a single hauler on the main stairway.
{count} arrivals confirmed. Among them, sources say, is at least one dwarf claiming to be a legendary cheesemaker. We are verifying.
More migrants tonight, as word spreads through {civ} that {fort} has ale. We're not saying it's the only reason. It's the main reason.
The newcomers have arrived wet, tired, and already unhappy about the lack of a statue garden. Welcome home, everyone.
Population up to {pop} after today's migrant wave. Food stockpile analysts are urging calm and, quietly, more farming.
{count} new dwarves, {count} new opinions about where the furniture should go. DNN welcomes them all.
Migrants arriving in winter, which veterans say is like turning up to a feast after the plates are cleared.

heads.text: ARE THEY ELVES? PLEASE DON'T BE ELVES

reads.text: A caravan has arrived at the depot. Traders are unpacking, and the broker is, as always, somewhere at the bottom of the fort carrying a rock.
Merchants are in {fort} this {season}. We're told they've brought cloth, leather, and the same overpriced barrel of pickles as last time.
Wagons are rolling in, viewers. If they are elves, please do not offer them anything made of wood. Again.
Traders from {civ} have reached the depot, and haulers are sprinting crafts up the stairs in what experts call a trinket stampede.
{citizen} has been named today's chief haggler, mostly because nobody else was standing near the depot.
The caravan is here. Merchants report the road was long, the weather was rough, and our gate was 'smaller than advertised.'
Breaking from the depot: the merchants want crafts. The fort has crafts. Decorated mugs are about to have a very big day.
Merchants have arrived. Ale analysts expect a run on imported drink, which is good, because ours is running low.
A caravan in {month}! Fort economists are calling it 'a lot of stuff', which is the technical term.
Trade season opens with the merchants camped at the depot and refusing to come any further in. We don't blame them. The stairs.
The caravan arrives as {fort} sits at {pop} citizens, all of whom, apparently, want to look at the merchants' animals.
Merchants are unloading now. {reporter} is on the scene and has already been talked into buying a cage they did not need.
Merchants at the gate, and the fort's negotiator is reportedly practising a 'disappointed face' in a polished stone wall.
The {year} trading season is open. Remember, viewers: everything at the depot is negotiable except the guards' patience.

heads.text: TALKS EXPECTED; MEETING ROOM NOT READY
DIPLOMACY BREAKS OUT IN THE FORT

reads.text: A diplomat has arrived in {fort}. Sources say they have requests, a tight schedule, and opinions about our trees.
The liaison from {civ} is here, asking how many of last season's agreements we honoured. Our answer is still being drafted.
A foreign envoy is at the gate. Staff have been asked to look busy, look friendly, and absolutely not mention the last envoy.
We're getting word of an official visit. Leadership is hurriedly furnishing an office. Any office. A chair will do.
The liaison has arrived, and is already asking to meet the expedition leader, who is currently hauling a bin of socks.
Diplomatic news this {season}: an envoy is in {fort}, and our negotiators are polishing their best 'we'll think about it.'
An elven diplomat, if reports are true, will soon ask us to stop cutting trees. Our woodcutters have been asked to stand casually.
The liaison from {civ} brings greetings from the mountainhome and, sources say, a list of things they'd like to buy cheaply.
A diplomat is touring {fort}. {citizen} was asked for comment and offered them a mug, which is about as diplomatic as it gets down here.
Breaking: a visitor with a seal on their papers. The fort's nobles are said to be thrilled. Everyone else is said to be hiding.
Talks begin today. On the table: trade, tribute, and whether the meeting room really needs to be next to the pig pen.
{reporter} tells us the envoy has been waiting at the gate for some time, and has started counting the bricks.
An envoy has come to {fort} in {month}. Historians note our diplomatic record is spotless, mostly because nobody wrote it down.
A diplomat at the depot, viewers. If you see them, smile, nod, and don't say the word 'tribute' near the bookkeeper.

heads.text: A NEW ARTIFACT FOR THE AGES
MOOD ENDS IN MASTERPIECE OF MASTERPIECES
THE WORKSHOP DOOR OPENS AT LAST
THE MOUNTAIN WILL REMEMBER THIS ONE
SCHOLARS, POETS AND BARDS ON STANDBY

reads.text: {name} has emerged from the workshop with a legendary {thing}. Witnesses describe it as 'very shiny' and 'not for sale, apparently.'
History tonight in {fort}: {name} has created an artifact. The {thing} has already been given a name longer than most of our corridors.
Breaking: an artifact! {name} spent days demanding materials, and the result, a legendary {thing}, has been declared worth every shriek.
We can confirm a legendary {thing} now exists in {fort}, crafted by {name}. Art critics are already arguing about the menacing spikes.
An artifact has been created in {fort}. The fort's value just went up, and so, sources warn, did its appeal to thieves.
{name} is a legend tonight. The new {thing} is decorated with images of, we're told, {name}. Modesty was not one of the materials.
Out of the strange mood and into the history books: {name} has finished. The {thing} is complete. The workshop is, frankly, a mess.
An artifact has been forged in {fort} this {season}. Scholars from across {civ} will soon arrive to look at it and say 'hmm.'
{citizen} was first to see the new artifact and has not stopped talking about it since. Nobody has the heart to interrupt.
Masterwork? No, viewers. Better. {name} has made a legendary {thing}, and the anchor desk has been asked not to lick it.
The legend of {name} begins today with a single {thing}. We expect the fort's poets to make this worse within the week.
An artifact in {fort}! Experts say it is now the most valuable object here, narrowly ahead of the last barrel of ale.
{name} has made something the world will talk about. The {thing} is now the fort's pride, its treasure, and its fire-safety concern.
Legendary craftsmanship confirmed in {year}. The artifact is being moved somewhere safe, which in this fort means 'a room with a door.'

heads.text: FORT'S PRIDE: ONE VERY GOOD ITEM

reads.text: {name} has produced a masterwork {thing}. Our panel will spend the next hour debating whether it's the best ever made. It is.
Breaking from the workshops: a masterpiece. {name} is said to be pleased, which for a dwarf means a very slight change in the eyebrows.
Tonight's top story is, and we cannot stress this enough, a very good {thing}. {name} made it. We're told it's perfect.
A masterwork has been crafted in {fort}. Experts confirm the quality is exceptional, and the craftsdwarf is already insufferable about it.
{name} has done it again. The masterwork {thing} joins a growing collection the fort has no idea where to store.
In craftsmanship news this {season}, a masterpiece. Critics praise the detail, the finish, and the fact that nobody got hurt.
Viewers, we have a masterwork. DNN will now describe the {thing} for the next eleven minutes. Settle in.
{citizen} has asked to touch the new masterwork. {name} has said no. Talks are ongoing.
Masterwork confirmed in {fort}. The skill on display has stunned onlookers and enraged at least two rival craftsdwarves.
{name} made a masterpiece today, and is said to have walked straight to the tavern afterwards. Professionals.
Our arts desk reports a masterwork {thing}, decorated with an image of a dwarf making that very {thing}. Very dwarf.
Another masterpiece out of {fort}. At this rate, the caravan will need a bigger wagon and a better appraiser.
A masterwork has been crafted, and the fort's mood has lifted measurably. A good object will do that. So will ale.
{name}'s new masterwork has already been called 'the finest in {civ}' by {name}, who sources say is not impartial.

heads.text: WILL IT BE A LEGEND, OR A TRAGEDY?

reads.text: {name} has been taken by a strange mood and has claimed a workshop. We're told nobody is to make eye contact.
We're getting reports {name} is staring at a wall and whispering about shells. If anyone has shells, now's the time.
A strange mood has struck in {fort}. The dwarf has locked themselves in a workshop. Experts urge patience and plenty of materials.
{name} is in a mood. Not a bad mood, viewers. A strange one. The fort's history may be about to change.
Breaking: {name} is demanding bones, gems and cloth, and will not say why. Sources say this is completely normal and also terrifying.
A dwarf has entered a fey mood this {season}. Workshop neighbours are asked to keep the noise down and the gems handy.
{citizen} reports seeing a dwarf sprint past with a wild look and an armful of leather. DNN can confirm: it's a mood.
{name} has gone quiet, focused, and slightly glowing. The next few days decide whether the fort gets an artifact or a funeral.
The mood has hit. Haulers are already being sent to the stockpiles for whatever {name} is pointing at.
Strange mood alert in {fort}. If a dwarf asks you for a specific rock, give them the rock. Don't ask about the rock.
Sources tell us {name} has been sketching on the workshop wall. The sketches are 'very intense' and 'possibly a helmet.'
A dwarf is in a mood, and the fort is holding its breath. {anchor2} has been told to stop guessing what it'll be. Live.
{name} has claimed a workshop and is refusing food, sleep and visitors. In other words, peak artistic process.
Mood watch, day one. {name} is demanding something nobody has. Fort logistics are pretending this is fine.

heads.text: WE NOW TAKE YOU TO THE PANIC
THE CAVERNS HAVE A NEW RESIDENT
ARE THE BRIDGES UP? DNN ASKS

reads.text: Breaking news: something enormous has been spotted near {fort}. Witnesses describe the {creature} as 'big', 'bigger', and 'no thank you.'
Stay indoors, viewers. A forgotten beast has emerged from the caverns, and it has, according to our caverns desk, far too many legs.
The {creature} is here. Commanders say they have a plan. Sources close to the military say the plan is mostly 'pull the lever.'
A monster is loose. {reporter} was going to cover this live but has asked, very sensibly, to cover it from far away.
Megabeast alert in {fort}. Citizens are reminded that the safest place to be is anywhere the {creature} isn't.
Something terrible has arrived this {season}. All {pop} citizens are urged to stay away from the cavern stairs. All of them.
We can confirm: {name} has arrived. The {creature} is said to be in a foul temper, which is reportedly its only temper.
Reports now that the {creature} is near the outer wall. The fort engineers would like it known they warned everyone about that wall.
A titan, a beast, a horror from below: details are scarce, but the screaming is consistent. DNN stays on air as long as there is air.
The {creature} has been seen in the caverns, and the fishers have been told that today, just this once, the carp are not the problem.
{citizen} saw it first and is resting comfortably in the hospital. Physically fine. Emotionally, still running.
Our monster correspondent says the {creature} breathes something unpleasant. Please do not find out what.
A beast has come to {fort}. The militia is mustering. The cats are hiding. The cats, as usual, are right.
The {creature} is the biggest thing to visit {fort} since the last biggest thing. We hope it leaves the same way: in pieces.
This is not a drill. Goblins have been sighted outside {fort}. Citizens are advised to move inside and, ideally, below.
An ambush has been sprung. Woodcutters are urged to drop the axes and run. Actually, keep the axes. Run with the axes.
A siege has begun. Our military correspondent says the goblins brought trolls, beak dogs and, worst of all, a drummer.
We're getting reports of {count} invaders on the road to {fort}. Every dwarf with a crossbow is now very popular.
Breaking: an enemy army is at the gates of {fort}. {citizen} has been seen dragging a barrel of ale to safety, and we salute that.
Goblins at the door, viewers. The militia commander asks civilians to please stop waving at them from the walls.
The siege is on. {fort}'s {pop} citizens are being herded below, where the ale is and the arrows aren't.
Invaders sighted this {season}. {reporter} is on the walls, and reports the goblins look 'grumpy' and 'very pointy.'
An ambush in {fort}! The attackers crept up quietly, which experts call unsporting and goblins call strategy.
War has come to {fort}. DNN will remain on air throughout the siege, partly out of duty, mostly because the studio is underground.
Goblins have arrived, and the trap corridor finally gets its moment. Engineers say they are 'nervous but very excited.'
The enemy is at the gates. Soldiers have been called up, the gate is shut, and the cook has sworn nobody is getting the roast.
A siege of {fort}. Analysts expect a long fight, a lot of arrows, and at least one dwarf who forgets to come inside.
{count} goblins confirmed. Our numbers desk would like to point out that's {count} more than we invited.
{name} has joined the military. The former {prof} will now swap tools for a weapon and a strict sparring schedule.
We can confirm {name} is now a soldier. Barracks sources say the recruit has already lost a fight with the training dummy.
The militia grows by one this {season}. Commanders say the new recruit is keen, alert and, for now, still smiling.
{name} the {prof} has traded the workshop for the barracks. Former colleagues say they'll miss the help and not the humming.
A citizen of {fort} has enlisted. Their first order: report to the barracks. Their second order: stop asking when lunch is.
{name} has been handed armour today. The armour, sources say, is slightly too big, and the recruit is pretending it isn't.
Another dwarf answers the call. {citizen} says the fort feels safer already, and also wonders who's doing the hauling now.
Military news: {name} is in the squad. Instructors say the recruit has 'potential' and 'a dangerous enthusiasm for axes.'
{name} has enlisted, bringing the fort's defenders up by one and its {prof} count down by one. Economists are still crunching that.
{fort} has a new soldier. Recruits are reminded the barracks are for sleeping, sparring, and not leaving socks on the weapon rack.
{name} reports for duty this {month}. Squadmates have already given them a nickname we cannot read on air.
A new recruit has joined the militia, which trains daily in the barracks. Neighbours report it is very loud and very stabby.
{name} is a soldier now. Family members describe themselves as proud, worried, and a little relieved about the bedroom space.
Enlistment news from {fort}: a dwarf who once flinched at a rat is now on the front line. Character growth, viewers.

heads.text: FROM THE BARRACKS TO THE BEDROOM
BACK TO WORK, BACK TO NORMAL

reads.text: {name} has left the military and returned to civilian life. The weapon goes back on the rack. The bad back, sources say, stays.
We can confirm {name} is a civilian again. First stop: the tavern. Second stop: also the tavern.
A soldier of {fort} has returned to civilian life this {season}. Friends say they look rested, and are already bored.
{name} has been discharged. Barracks staff are reportedly sad to see them go and pleased to get the bunk back.
{name} is out of uniform and back to work as the fort's {prof}. Colleagues have hidden the training dummy, out of kindness.
Militia numbers fall by one after a dwarf returned to civilian work. Commanders say the squad will manage. The squad says it won't.
{citizen} tells DNN a returning soldier has already asked twice where the good chairs went. Welcome home.
Life after service begins for {name}. Veterans warn the hardest part is remembering to walk, not march, to dinner.
{name} has handed back the armour. The armour has been described as 'smelly but honourable.'
A soldier comes home to civilian life in {fort}. Their first civilian decision: a long nap. A very long nap.
Discharge papers confirmed for {name}. Historians will note this {month} as the month one dwarf finally put the shield down.
Breaking from the barracks: one fewer soldier, one more hauler. The fort's furniture is about to get moved very fast.
{name} has rejoined civilian life, and is reportedly startled by how quiet it is when nobody's shouting drills.
Civilian life welcomes back one of the fort's defenders. Peace reigns, for now, and the militia lounge has a spare cushion.

heads.text: THE NOBLE GETS THEIR WAY AGAIN

reads.text: The noble's mandate has been fulfilled. Citizens are relieved, workshops are exhausted, and the noble has already thought of another one.
Production quota met in {fort}. The hammerer has been seen putting the hammer away, slightly disappointed.
A noble's demand has been satisfied this {season}. The items in question are, we're told, completely useless. That's not the point.
{name} delivered the final piece of the mandate. The noble said nothing, which in noble terms is effusive praise.
Mandate met. Workshop crews are celebrating with a drink, and the noble is celebrating by banning the export of something.
We can report the fort has filled its quota. Analysts say it's the first time this {year} everyone involved slept the night before.
The order is done. Sources close to the noble say they 'expected nothing less', which sources close to the workshops call a lie.
{name} completed the job that satisfied the noble. The fort owes them a mug, and quite possibly its kneecaps.
Quota fulfilled. {citizen} says the whole fort can finally stop making that one particular item. Until next time.
A mandate completed in {fort}, just in time. Observers say the deadline was so tight you could hear the forges sweating.
The noble's production order has been met. Historians expect the noble to forget about it entirely by the end of the season.
Good news from the workshops: the mandate is done. {anchor2} is asking what the mandate was. Nobody remembers. It doesn't matter.
Thanks to {name}, the quota is filled. The noble asked to see the work, glanced at it, and asked for a nicer chair.
Quota met. The jail stays empty, the hammer stays on the hook, and the fort, for one more day, stays on the noble's good side.

heads.text: A MATCH MADE IN THE TAVERN

reads.text: {name} is married. The happy couple were seen sharing a mug at the tavern, which is the dwarven equivalent of a ceremony.
Love has won in {fort} this {season}. Two citizens are now married, and the bedroom district has one less awkward hallway nod.
Wedding news: {name} has tied the knot. Friends say they met over a disagreement about masonry and never stopped arguing. Romantic.
Breaking: a marriage in {fort}! We're told no ceremony was held, because dwarves don't do ceremonies. They do ale.
{name} is officially off the market. The rest of the fort is said to be very happy for them and slightly jealous.
{citizen} has been seen weeping into a tankard over today's wedding, saying they 'always knew'. They did not always know.
Two dwarves have married this {month}. The fort's matchmakers, which is to say everyone in the tavern, are taking credit.
{name} has married. DNN understands the couple will share a bedroom, a bed, and at least one fierce argument about the blanket.
Romance in {fort}! Experts say the newlyweds' love is as solid as granite, and roughly as easy to talk to.
{name} has wed. The couple's first act as a married pair was to request a bigger bedroom, which the fort has denied.
Love in the time of thin rations. {name} is married. We wish them a long life and a better-stocked pantry.
Wedding bells, figuratively, for {name}. Literally, the fort has no bells. Engineering would like to build some. Please stop them.
Wedding news for a {year} to remember. The newlyweds are blissful, and the fort's bards have already written something regrettable.
{name} is married, ending one of the longest courtships in {fort} history. Onlookers describe it as 'finally' and 'about time.'

heads.text: POWER CHANGES HANDS IN THE FORT
SOMEBODY GET THIS DWARF AN OFFICE

reads.text: {name} has been appointed to a new post. Their first official act was asking for a bigger bedroom. Their second, a bigger one still.
Election news from {fort}: {name} has won. Turnout was high, mostly because the polling station was the tavern.
A new appointment in {fort} this {season}. Citizens are cautiously optimistic, which is the only kind of optimism allowed down here.
{name} takes office today. Sources say the new noble has already drafted three mandates and a strongly worded note about chairs.
We can confirm {name} is the fort's newest official. The former {prof} says power won't change them, while adjusting a new robe.
Someone has been elected or appointed in {fort}. We don't fully understand how the process works. Neither, it turns out, does anyone.
{name} has a new title. Engravers are working overtime adding it to doors, walls, and, at {name}'s request, the ceiling.
Breaking: power has changed hands. {citizen} says the new noble 'seems nice', which is what everyone says before the first mandate.
The {year} political season brings a new face to the top. Furniture makers are bracing for very specific demands.
{name} has been named to office. Their predecessor has been seen in the tavern, looking ten years younger.
A new noble in {fort}. The bookkeeper has added them to the list of dwarves who need gold-plated things.
{name} accepted the new post this {month} with a short speech. It was mostly about the size of the office.
There's a new official in town. DNN reminds them that we are an independent network, and also very, very fond of them.
{name}'s appointment is official. Reaction ranges from 'who?' to 'oh no' to, from one cousin, 'finally.'

heads.text: A STORY YOU NEED TO HEAR

reads.text: We interrupt our coverage with breaking news from {fort}. Details are still coming in. Something has definitely happened.
This just in: an announcement has been made. DNN's analysts are reading it now. Slowly. Moving their lips.
We're getting reports from around {fort}. {reporter} is standing by, although we're not sure where, or why they're wet.
Developing story, viewers. {citizen} tells DNN it is 'quite something.' We'll be the judge of that.
News from {fort} this {season}. We don't know much yet, but sources close to the ale stockpile are confident it's important.
Breaking: a development in {fort}. Our team is on it. Our team is two dwarves and a cat, but they're on it.
An announcement has gone out across the fort. All {pop} citizens are advised to keep calm and keep hauling.
Something has happened in {fort}, viewers. Is it good? Is it bad? Stay with DNN, where we'll tell you as soon as we decide.
We are receiving word of a development. {anchor2} has a theory. We will not be hearing {anchor2}'s theory.
News out of {fort} in {month}. The newsroom is gathered around the announcement board, squinting.
Here's what we know: something happened. Here's what we don't know: everything else. More after this.
{anchor} with breaking news. The fort has made an announcement, and the official word is that it is, technically, news.
A new development in {fort}, and possibly the biggest story of {year}. {citizen} was nearby and looked surprised.
The announcement board has spoken. DNN has sent {reporter} to find out what it said, and whether it can be blamed on elves.

death.text: Terrible. Just terrible. I'll be at the tavern if anyone needs to not talk about it.
{name} once fixed my door hinge without being asked. I never said thank you. Say thank you, viewers.
I don't have a joke for this one, {anchor}. I don't think the fort wants one.
Rest easy, {name}. The stone will remember you, even if the bookkeeper gets the date wrong.
We'll all be wearing our second-best beard tonight, as is custom.
I've been told to say something profound. All I've got is: drink one for them.
That's {pop} of us now. Every one of them counts, {anchor}.
The fort will carry on. That's what forts do. But it'll carry on a little slower today.
I hope the coffin's a good one. {name} would have checked the joins.
A moment of silence, then. Well. A moment of captions.

pet_death.text: I'm not crying, {anchor}. It's the smoke from the smelter.
Every {creature} deserves a better send-off than the bone pile. Just saying.
I'd like to remind viewers the butcher is a professional and should not be glared at. Excessively.
Somebody check on the owner. And maybe pick out a nice wall for them.
The cats are going to be unbearable about this.
I once shared a pasture bench with {name}. Quiet animal. Great listener.
Losing an animal is hard. Losing one right before dinner is complicated.
Rest easy, {name}. You were a good {creature}. Mostly.
Pour one out. Into the trough, I mean. Respectfully.

birth.text: Oh, that's lovely. That's actually lovely. Somebody get that baby a tiny helmet.
Another mouth to feed, and I mean that with all the joy in my heart.
Congratulations, {name}! Sleep is overrated. You'll find that out shortly.
I give it six years before it's demanding a bedroom with an engraved ceiling.
New dwarf smell. Best smell in the mountain.
Can we get a camera on the baby? No? Guild rules? Fine.
Good. The fort needs more dwarves who haven't learned to complain yet.
{pop} of us now. Somebody tell the brewer.
I hope it grows up to be a legendary something. Anything. I'm not fussy.
A happy day in {fort}. I'm going to need a minute. And a drink.

migrants.text: More dwarves! Great. I'll start hiding my good chair.
I just hope they brought their own mugs.
{count}? I counted more beards than that. Some of them might have two.
Somebody show them the dining hall before they start eating the seeds.
Welcome, everyone. Please don't ask me where the bedrooms are. Nobody knows.
Every one of them is a future legend, {anchor}. Or a future hauler. Mostly haulers.
I give them a week before they're complaining about the stairs like real citizens.
Can any of them brew? Ask them if any of them brew.
Big day for the fort. Bigger day for the bookkeeper.
Ah, migrants. Fresh, untroubled, unaware of the carp.

caravan.text: I'm going to buy something useless and I want everyone to know I'm happy about it.
Did they bring any cheese? I'm asking for the whole fort.
If it's elves, I'm calling in sick.
Somebody find the broker. Somebody always has to find the broker.
Last caravan I came home with a single cave spider silk sock. Just the one.
Big day for the craftsdwarves. Every rock mug in the fort is about to be 'artisanal.'
They always look so tired when they get here. Then they see our prices and perk right up.
Remember, {anchor}: you don't need it. You want it. There's a difference. I've never respected it.
I hope they take beds. We've made so many beds.
Ah, the sweet sound of wagon wheels and someone shouting 'that's not what we agreed.'

diplomat.text: Make sure they see the good engravings. Hide the one of the goblin.
Diplomacy. Ah yes. Talking until somebody gets bored and signs something.
If it's an elf, I volunteer to be very, very polite. From a different room.
I hope we're not at war after this. Last time somebody served the wrong cheese.
Can they stay for dinner? We've got roast. We've always got roast.
I love a diplomat. Always somewhere important to be, never anywhere to sleep.
Someone should tell them about the carp. As a courtesy.
Let's not get excited, {anchor}. Last one only wanted to know where the toilets were. We don't have toilets.
That's {civ} for you. Always sending someone with a scroll.
Our relations are excellent, according to us.

artifact.text: Can I hold it? Just for a second? No? Okay.
I've seen it. I wept. Then I had to sit down. Then I wept again.
Good for {name}. I was worried that mood was going to end the other way.
That {thing} is going in the history books, {anchor}. Possibly also a display case. Probably also a thief's bag.
Every dwarf dreams of making one of these. I dream of being allowed near one.
They're going to write songs about this. Bad songs. Long songs.
Nobody use it. You can't use an artifact. It's an artifact.
Legendary! In our little fort! I'm genuinely proud and slightly worried about goblins.
{name} deserves a feast. And a nap. Mostly a nap.
And to think, a week ago that was just a pile of bones and screaming.

masterpiece.text: It's a {thing}, {anchor}. But it's a really, really good {thing}.
I'd cry, but I'd hate to get it wet.
Masterwork. Even the word sounds expensive.
My mug has never once been a masterpiece. I'm happy for {name}. I'm also jealous.
Someone frame it. Can you frame a {thing}? Someone try.
That's the kind of thing that cheers a fort right up.
If the merchants try to buy it, I say we act like we don't hear them.
Ten out of ten. No notes. Well, one note: put it somewhere I can see it.
Every masterwork makes me want to take up a craft. Then I remember the hours.
{name} won't shut up about it now. And honestly? Fair.

mood.text: Oh, I love a mood. Unless it's the bad kind. Is it the bad kind?
Somebody give {name} whatever they want. Please. All of it.
Last time this happened we got a legendary bracelet. A bracelet, {anchor}.
I'm going to say what we're all thinking: I hope it's a weapon.
Don't look directly at them. Bad luck. Or rude. One of those.
I'd go into a strange mood too if I worked in that workshop.
Do we have the materials? Please tell me we have the materials.
Every mood is a coin flip. Legend on one side. Screaming on the other.
I'm bringing {name} a snack. I'll leave it at the door and run.
Our thoughts are with the workshop. And the bones in it.

beast.text: I'd like to request a transfer to the deepest room. Or the highest. Whichever's furthest from that.
Can we raise the bridge while we're talking? Can someone do that? Right now?
The militia's got this. The militia has got this. Please, militia, have this.
I'm not saying panic. I'm saying panic thoughtfully.
If it's made of fire, I'm out. If it's made of steam, I'm also out.
Ah, the {creature}. My least favourite thing, effective immediately.
Has anyone told it we're a news network? Maybe it respects the press.
Every time something crawls out of the caverns I think, that's the worst one. Then another one crawls out.
Well, we'll always have the trap hallway.

siege.text: Goblins. Of course it's goblins. It's always goblins.
I'd like it on record that I said we needed a bigger wall.
Give 'em the trap hall! Give 'em the whole trap hall!
I'm brave. I'm very brave. I'm going to be brave from the deep tavern.
Has someone pulled the lever? Somebody tell me someone's pulled the lever.
{anchor}, if I don't make it, I want my mug to go to the museum.
The goblins think they're scary. They've never seen our militia commander before breakfast.
Why do they always come during dinner?
I just hope they don't reach the ale stockpile. Everything else can be replaced.
Strike the earth? Strike the goblins, more like.

soldier.text: Good for {name}. Every fort needs someone willing to stand between us and the goblins.
I tried the militia once. I lasted one sparring session and one very bad bruise.
Welcome to the squad. Your armour is wherever the last soldier left it.
I hope {name} kept a few tools. Never know when you'll need to fix a door mid-siege.
They look good in a helmet. Everyone looks good in a helmet.
That's one more dwarf who'll sleep in the barracks and complain about the barracks.
Fight well, {name}. And spar gently. You'll be sparring with your friends.
We should do a feature on the new recruits. From a respectful distance.
Militia life. Up early, sore all day, hungry all night. Sounds like journalism.
Salute! Did I do that right? I've never done that.

civilian.text: Enjoy it, {name}. You've earned your mug and your chair.
I hope they keep the helmet. You never know.
Back to normal life. Normal life in this fort. Good luck.
Somebody give them a nice quiet job. Not the hospital. Not the depot. Somewhere quiet.
From soldier to civilian. It's like a promotion, but with more naps.
I'll miss seeing {name} marching past the newsroom at dawn. I won't miss the clanking.
Quietest discharge I've ever seen. Usually somebody cries. Usually it's the commander.
Thank you for your service, {name}. Now go have a drink.
Fewer soldiers makes me nervous. More haulers makes me happy. I'm conflicted.
That's what we like to see: a dwarf leaving the army in one piece.

quota.text: Thank the stone. I was not ready for another hammering.
What was the mandate? Doesn't matter. It's done. Let's never speak of it.
Another mandate down. Another one's coming. They always come back.
Nobles, eh? Can't live with them, can't legally drop them in the magma.
I'd like to thank the workshops. And I'd like the workshops to have a nap.
Good work, {name}. You've saved someone's knees today.
The noble is happy. Write that down. It won't last.
Every time we meet a quota I feel like we've won something. We haven't. We just didn't lose.
They'll want gold cups next. Mark my words. Gold cups.
Quota met, crisis over. Back to our regularly scheduled crises.

marriage.text: Oh, that's adorable. I'm going to be insufferable about weddings all week.
May your ale never run dry and your bedroom never flood.
Congratulations, {name}! Nothing says love like sharing a stone bed.
I'm genuinely touched. And single. But touched.
Babies next, I suppose. I'll alert the carpenters.
I hope they have a long, happy, slightly argumentative life together.
A marriage! During all this! Good for them.
We should send a gift. Do we have a gift? We have a rock.
Love really does find a way. Even through three layers of granite.
To the happy couple. May they never be assigned the same workshop.

noble.text: I give it three days before the first mandate. Two, if they've seen the good stone.
Congratulations, {name}. Please don't ban anything I like.
Power. Responsibility. Very specific furniture requirements.
I voted for them. I think. I wasn't really paying attention.
Remember us little dwarves, {name}. Remember the press.
They'll want a throne next. Mark my words.
Well, somebody's got to do it. I'm just glad it's not me.
New noble, same old demands. That's democracy. Or monarchy. Whatever this is.
I hope they like the job. Nobody ever likes the job.
Somebody warn the masons. The room requirements are coming.

generic.text: Well. That's certainly a thing that happened.
I'll be honest, {anchor}, I didn't follow that, but I'm very concerned.
Is that good news? It sounded like good news. I'm going with good news.
This is why I got into journalism. That, and the free ale.
I'm going to need a full panel on this. And a snack.
Hard to believe. Easy to report.
The fort never sleeps. Well. The fort sleeps a lot. The news never sleeps.
Let's get {reporter} on the line. Do we have a line? We have a tube.
Truly a historic moment for {fort}. One of several this week.
